source.title: Linear RNNs Provably Learn Linear Dynamic Systems
source.authors: Li-Fu Wang; Tianyu Wang; Shengwei Yi; Bo Shen; Bo Hu; Xing Cao

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; it is a theoretical study of linear recurrent networks and stable linear dynamical systems, not the benchmark classification settings named in the claim.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves gradient-based learning guarantees for a related non-convex network training problem, but studies linear RNN system identification rather than the claim's classification-error settings.
record.gate_note: Theorem 4 and the conclusion report an SGD guarantee for fitting stable linear systems with a convex loss. These results bear on the broad claim about gradient training in non-convex networks, but not directly on the listed benchmark, depth, initialization-comparison, learning-rate, normalization, or width conditions. The paper reports no CIFAR, classification-error, corrupted-label, or random-label experiments.
record.test_reason: The study proves convergence guarantees for linear RNN system identification. None of its own results tests V1–V6: sufficient width and a prescribed initialization do not establish the specific width or initialization comparisons those versions describe. Its discussion of two-layer ReLU local minima cites prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: the authors claim a theoretical SGD learning guarantee for stable linear systems using sufficiently wide, suitably randomly initialized linear RNNs, with required width independent of sequence length. The guarantee also depends on accuracy, confidence, the stability envelope constant and other stated assumptions; width does not depend only on ρC.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes theoretical SGD training of linear RNNs for stable linear system identification, rather than benchmark classification training or the recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantee depends on sufficient width, the stable-system condition ||C^k D|| ≤ cρ ρC^k, and the specified random initialization; the paper's theorem states its bounds do not depend on input sequence length T.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 4 bounds the average online sequence-loss excess over an admissible stable target system by O(ϵ), with high probability, for sufficiently wide linear RNNs trained using the prescribed SGD recipe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under explicit stability, bounded-data, loss, initialization and width assumptions, SGD learns stable linear dynamical systems with polynomial sample and iteration complexity.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 6 and Corollary 7 extend the guarantee to population sequence loss relative to the stable-system comparator class.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated assumptions, trained linear RNNs achieve population sequence loss at most OPTρC + O(ϵ), with high probability.

record.problems: The evidence is a theoretical guarantee under explicit assumptions, not an empirical benchmark study. The excerpt does not give empirical validation of the theorem or compare alternative initialization, width, depth, normalization, or learning-rate recipes.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results identified. Related-work results cited from other papers were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Convolutional classification training error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels, model size, stopping and regularization conditions.
Spurious-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Training degradation with convolutional depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts, special tanh initialization or Fixup.
Comparative training speed and trainable depth under activation-matched initializations, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and deep convolutional kernels.
Loss recovery above initial stability thresholds, curvature changes, edge-of-stability trajectories and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The theoretical results are valid adjacent findings to retain, but they warrant no verdict on V1–V6. The statement that the loss framework can cover classification does not supply a classification-error result.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, corrupted or random labels, convolutional models, and smaller models or regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network depth effects on classification training error, including normalization and shortcut comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, gradient propagation comparisons, and very deep tanh or convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss rise and recovery, sharpness trajectories, and divergence conditions.
Batch-normalization effects on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.measure: Average empirical sequence loss gap relative to the target system
rows.note: Guarantee is for stable linear system identification and a loss gap, not classification error. The excerpted theorem statement is split across paper text; the paper describes the bound as applying for sufficiently large width and polynomial iterations.
rows.check: Theorem 4, Eq. (12), bounds the average online loss difference across SGD iterates and sampled sequences relative to an admissible target system, not directly OPTρC or a final model's training loss. Algorithm 1 initializes the trained recurrent matrix with variance ρ/m; variance 1/m applies to the rescaled W0. B remains fixed. This guarantee cannot determine any listed version's effect.
